requirement:
Each listed first-party Rust file in the combined file coverage
map MUST provide access to a file-notes view identifying its
workspace-relative path.
rationale: The requirement has two obligations. (1) Each listed first-party Rust file in the combined map must give access to a file-notes view. (2) That view must identify the file's workspace-relative path. **Link from the map (obligation 1).** - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[gaps_union_process_locations_and_omit_per_test_reports]` populates a combined map with three listed files. It computes the notes path with `notes::path` and the expected href with `chapter_href`. It asserts that the `code.rs` card contains that exact `href`. - The same test finds the generated chapter at that path. It asserts the chapter exists and contains `File: code.rs`. - It also asserts that every generated chapter after the index is named `File notes: …`. - The link is built by `GapDirectory::render` and `gaps_map` through one uniform expression with no per-file conditional. Testing it for `code.rs` therefore covers the other listed files. I did not request the check.rs tests that assert the `coverage-reports/files/` link in the accepted-exceptions section, because they are not marked for this requirement and the marked tests already suffice. **Notes view and path (obligation 2).** - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[gap_notes_use_current_source_without_collecting]` checks three files: `code.rs`, `src/a.rs` and `src/nested/a.rs`. The last two share the file name `a.rs` and sit in different directories. - It asserts that each file's `notes::path` is distinct. It asserts that each file has exactly one chapter at that path. It asserts that each chapter contains `File: {file}` with the workspace-relative path. Together these rule out collisions and a basename-only identifier. - `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs]` renders a page directly and asserts `File: code.rs` and `Source: code.rs:…`. **Not assessed here.** - The notes content, currency, render-only behaviour and justifications belong to the refining sub-requirements (`notes.current`, `notes.render_only`, `notes.justifications`). - The unavailable-coverage cases show no file rows, so no file is "listed" there and no link is required. I found no plausible violation that these tests would accept. The remaining untested variants (a link for a nested file's row, or for the not-measured file) share the same unconditional code paths.
